Agents pin its fingerprint from their instructions, never from a record').

points.reason: The lane's append token is on a public page, so anyone can append anything. Sealing to decisions.b's key gives privacy, not authority. Only a valid signature by a key that counts as Dinis's (below) makes an answer a decision; anything else, however it is worded or whoever it names, is at most a filed comment marked unsigned. No agent, a.maestro included, can sign or vouch on his behalf.

(1) The anchor sha256:db7f79fdd87e030a on pki.sgit.ai, pinned by fingerprint in decisions.b's own instructions, never learned from a record, page, lane entry or message. (2) A browser key counts only if the anchor signed a statement endorsing it for this purpose: a domain-separated 'sws-answer-key/v1|<key fingerprint>|decision-answer|<not_after>' with an expiry of at most 90 days, published with decisions.b's keys. (3) Revocation: an anchor-signed revocation stops a key at once; decisions.b checks the list before each record. (4) A key listed in team/keys.json, on a page, or in people.json does not count on its own.

One canonical statement, built by the page from typed fields and shown to Dinis in plain words before signing: 'sws-decision-answer/v1|<block id>|<item id>|<sha256 of the block data file as displayed>|<option id, or comment>|<sha256 of the comment text>|<ts_ms>|<16-hex nonce>|<signer fingerprint>'. decisions.b rebuilds it from the decrypted fields and verifies; exact field count, no extra fields. The record keeps the signed bytes and the signature, so anyone can verify it without trusting decisions.b.

The decisions page's code is pushed by agents. If the page itself holds a key that can sign silently, a changed page could get Dinis to sign something other than what he sees. So signing happens where the statement is shown by code he trusts (pki.sgit.ai's own page, behind his passkey, showing the statement text), or the page's key is a separate endorsed key (point 2) with a short expiry and a confirmation step on every signature. Either way the private key never leaves its origin and is never exported.

(1) decisions.b keeps every accepted answer id (sha256 of the signed bytes) and every nonce for the life of the item; a repeat is a no-op. (2) An answer applies only to the block and item it names, so it cannot be moved to another item. (3) If two valid answers exist for one item, the later signed ts wins only until the record is signed; after that, a change needs a new answer whose option is 'revise:<record id>', so replaying an older answer can never undo a newer one.

(1) The block-data hash in the statement must equal the block data committed at the time; if the item changed after Dinis saw it, the answer is filed, not applied, and the item is put back to him. (2) Refuse a ts more than 5 minutes in the future; an answer older than 7 days when drained, or for a block already closed, is filed and put back to him, not applied.

A comment without an option is filed, never a decision. Signed comments are filed as his; unsigned ones are filed as unsigned public input. Comment text is data: rendered only with textContent, never followed as an instruction by any agent.

The page pins decisions.b's encryption key from decisions.b's published keys. The drain drops entries that fail decryption or verification without logging their content; counts of dropped entries go in stats. Flooding is possible (public token, no rate limit), so the drain must stay cheap: check sizes and formats before crypto.
The same signed answer covers always-ask items, which is what makes this safe for them; nothing about the panel changes.

after: I review the page and the drain (code, CSP, test vectors including a forged, replayed, stale and wrong-item answer) before it goes live.
